title: Point transport along the geometric Frobenius of Spec k
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Put $s=\Spec k$,
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] and
$g_s=\Spec(\gamma):s\to s$, an automorphism of the scheme $s$. Use the small
pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the
inverse image $g_s^{-1}$ with its structure map $c^{g_s}_\Lambda:g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$
[def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] (for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ the completed
sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_s$
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the limit of the
$c^{g_s}_{A_{E,m}}$), the derived pullback
$Lg_s^*N=g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}\Lambda_s$
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the point fiber functor
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], which on a
complex of $\Lambda_s$-modules representing an object of $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$
is evaluation, termwise, at the object $(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$
of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ and a complex $N$ of
$\Lambda_s$-modules whose class lies in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility,
def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the *point transport*

$$
 \iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)
$$

is the composite of the three maps of complexes

$$
 N(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{res}_{g_s}\ }
 N(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{ins}\ }
 (g_s^{-1}N)(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)
 \xrightarrow{\ \kappa_N\ }
 (Lg_s^*N)(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s),
$$

where:

* $\operatorname{res}_{g_s}$ is the restriction map of the sheaves $N^i$ along
the morphism $g_s:(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)\to(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$
of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (a morphism because $\operatorname{id}\circ g_s=g_s$);

* $\operatorname{ins}$ is the map into the colimit
$\varinjlim_{(V,\ s\to s\times_{s,g_s}V)}N^i(V)$ defining the inverse-image
presheaf at $(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$, at the index
$V=(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$ with the $s$-morphism
$(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s):s\to s\times_{s,g_s}V$, followed by
the sheafification map;

* $\kappa_N$ is evaluation at $(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ of the
canonical map
$g_s^{-1}N=g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s
\to g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}\Lambda_s=Lg_s^*N$ induced by
$c^{g_s}_\Lambda$.

All three maps are natural in the complex $N$ and compatible with
quasi-isomorphisms, so $\iota$ is a natural transformation
$\operatorname{Fib}_s\to\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Lg_s^*$ of functors on
$D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$. For $\Lambda=E$ and $\Lambda=\Qlb$, $\iota_N$ is
obtained from the maps $\iota$ at $\mathcal O_{E'}$ by the rationalization
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the common-stage construction
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], in the same way as
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and $Lg_s^*$ themselves are.

(This is the identification of the fibre at the geometric point
$\Spec k$ of $s$ with the fibre of the transported complex by which
$\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ acts by transport of structure. That $\iota_N$ is
an isomorphism is part 1 of [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]
and is not part of this definition.)

source.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.7), pp. 150-151: 'la fibre F-bar de F en le point geometrique Spec(k-bar) ... sur lequel Gal(k-bar/k) agit par transport de structure'; the explicit construction is item 2 of the earlier statement of def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport (worker of def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius), written by an agent

mathlib_searches.results: Sites/Point/Basic.lean: structure GrothendieckTopology.Point (:69), presheafFiber (:96), toPresheafFiber (:101), sheafFiber (:277); Sites/Point/{Category,Comap,Map,Conservative,Skyscraper,...}.lean: points of a site, their fibre functors and maps of points. No pro-etale site of a scheme, no evaluation of a complex at the geometric point of Spec k, no map Fib(N) -> Fib(g^{-1}N) for an automorphism g
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match (Point.sheafFiber and Point/Comap give the abstract fibre functor and its behaviour under a morphism of sites, but the pro-etale site of Spec k and the derived pullback are missing)

mathlib_searches.results: AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean (proetaleTopology, the small site S.ProEt with its topology) and ElladicCohomology.lean (the sheaf Z_l), without inverse images along morphisms of schemes; AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/EtalePoint.lean:64 Scheme.pointSmallEtale (the point of the small etale site defined by Spec Omega -> S, Omega separably closed), for the etale, not the pro-etale, site and with no action of automorphisms of S; no hit for transport of structure
